div.style: text-align: left;
text-align: left;
div.span: - Satan is a fallen angel who freely rebelled against God out of pride, being entirely motivated in drawing others into his rebellion.
- He is the ruler of this world, the god of this age, and the prince of power of the air - holding the world in a kind of spiritual captivity through deception, lies, and fear of death.

div.style: text-align: left;
div.span: - His power is strictly derivative and limited: he can only act by God's permission, and Christ's death and resurrection are the decisive defeat of his dominion - guaranteeing his condemnation in the lake of fire.

div.style: text-align: left;
text-align: left;

div.span: - Islam then changes Satan into being a jinn who fell from his earned, angel-like status - now enitirely motivated in dragging as many of us as possible into hell with him, out of envy of God's honoring of mankind.

div.style: text-align: left;
div.span: - He can only whisper and tempt implicitly by deception, lies, appealing to our desires, and beautifying falsehood - all by God's permission.

div.style: text-align: left;

div.style: text-align: left;

font.b: Christianity looks more like a corrupted version of Islam, while Islam looks more like a corrected version of Christianity

div.font: Both religions affirm that God is One, ultimately loving, perfectly just and merciful, that He values and merits righteousness, and that He alone permits everything - including both our own wills and Satan’s influence. However, they manifest these same truths in very different ways, leading to fundamentally significant differences. As a result, this question does not deny the existence of any of these attributes on either side, but rather explores the nuances in how they manifest - allowing us to identify which drift (from one to the other) more closely matches with how a deceiver would act (when assuming one side is fully True).

If we assume Christianity is the original truth, then Islam's differences look like a drift that sharpens God's oneness and rationality, magnifies mercy and accountability, and diminishes the emphasis on Satan's power. Likewise, if we assume Islam is the original truth, then Christianity's differences look like a drift that increases God's expectations, emphasizes Satan's power, reduces God's oneness and original mercy, and diminishes the salvific function of our good deeds, our spiritual status, and rationality. Neither one sacrifices God's justice, grace, and the reality of the law - merely redirecting how they manifest, as they are entirely coherent (within their own narratives).

From this comparison, it is clear that a deceiver would align more with corrupting Islam into Christianity. In line with previous sections' conclusions, Islam presents a more consistent divine system: God's transcendence is greater (without sacrificing intimate closeness), rationality is sharper (without denying mystery or our limits), God's mercy is immediate (as Christianity delays the application of Jesus' atonement with Adam's sin), and righteousness and repentance are valued over sin (without removing our accountability or sin's ability to condemn). Even our status is more honored in Islam, with Adam being forgiven from his sin and us being born pure (rather than being punished and entering into a fallen state - like Satan did in both narratives).

So, if a deceiver wants to misguide from the truth as much as possible, then reducing God's transcendence, mercy, and rationality, lowering our status, elevating Satan's emphasis, and redirecting our faith and hope in a way that God did not authorize all align with the transition from Islam to Christianity (making Islam look like Christianity's correction).

switch.text: Christianity looks more like a corrupted version of Islam, while Islam looks more like a corrected version of Christianity...
